A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and complete appendices. The appendices can be matched, including v2 Appendices I–K becoming v3 Appendices J–L after insertion of the SGD appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original SGD experiments on pure-noise and single-index data in Figures 2 and 4, Gaussian-model GD simulations in Figures 6–7, and numerical DMFT results throughout the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and numerical analyses, and additionally displays training-error trajectories in Figure 10.

M1.justification: The two-layer model, gradient-flow dynamics, initialization regimes, Gaussian approximation, and central DMFT equations are retained. The expanded explanations and SGD implementation appendix document existing procedures rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic pure-noise fitting, single-index regression, and Gaussian-process surrogate simulations. The added Figure 10 panel remains within the existing pure-noise scenario.

E2.justification: The SGD/GD-versus-DMFT validations and comparisons with mean-field and asymptotic predictions retain the same comparison methods. Figure 24 corrects the label of an existing mean-field curve without replacing the comparator.

E3.justification: No revision to the retained experiments' evaluation design is established. The interpolation-threshold procedure, including its 10^-7 error threshold, is unchanged. Newly reported SGD settings describe the existing Figures 2 and 4; Figure 10 displays trajectories underlying the retained analysis.

E4.justification: Figure 10 adds direct training-error decay curves across alpha values, providing additional diagnostic evidence for the exponential-relaxation assumption used in the existing interpolation-threshold analysis. The numerical-accuracy checks and finite-width analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 newly specifies that Figures 2 and 4 average ten simulations, also stated in Appendix I. This is newly disclosed averaging information, not evidence of increased runs. The 10^4-realization reporting for Figures 6–7 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 10 newly reports training-error trajectories for alpha from 0.05 to 0.65 at gamma0 = 10/7. The existing interpolation thresholds 0.835, 0.605, and 0.262, fitted exponent 2, and previously plotted experimental curves are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 revises the bounds to include sqrt(k) and noise dependence, makes the generalization bound two-sided, and drops its explicit probability qualifier. Appendix J.1 expands the concentration argument. Other local changes correct the width limit in Section 2.4, add a test-error expression in Section 3, and change the covariance decomposition from minus in v2 (K.11) to plus in v3 (L.11). The central DMFT framework and timescale conclusions remain.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly adds large sample count per input dimension, n/d, alongside large width as a condition for the timescale-separation claim. This refines the stated scope while retaining the four principal contributions concerning complexity, inductive bias, decoupling, and feature unlearning.

C2.justification: Section 2.3 qualifies the signal/noise interpolation-threshold relation as expected rather than simply asserting it. Section 4 adds the expectation that the findings explain benefits of second-layer regularization. The principal interpretations and acknowledged uncertainty about long-time scaling remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix I supplies model and optimizer code, initialization and projection descriptions, batch size 100, step size 0.1, and zero momentum and weight decay for existing SGD simulations. Figure 2 newly specifies d = 200 and alpha = 0.4. Appendix D.1 adds response-function discretization details. These are documentation additions, with some internal inconsistencies.

R1.justification: v3 adds Ben Arous, Gheissari, and Jagannath (2021), connecting the existing nonzero linear-correlation assumption to information exponent one. It also explains more explicitly why the Gaussian approximation is used instead of the more complex existing exact DMFT characterization.

P1.justification: The title changes, a detailed contents section is added, several main-text explanations are expanded, vague supplementary-material references become specific appendix references, and the discussion's answers to research questions are separated. The main narrative and appendix organization otherwise remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 10 expands to two panels. Figure 3's caption removes an incorrect inset description, and Figure 24's legend changes from an error label to the appropriate mean-field projection label. Code blocks and the contents listing are added; other figures are retained with layout shifts.

improvement.justification: v3 improves navigation, implementation disclosure, and parts of the mathematical exposition, including the covariance-sign correction. However, its new response discretization in D.1 has the opposite impulse sign to retained equation (C.10), and the new Section 3 test-error formula omits the noise term retained in (G.46). Theorem 1 also loses its explicit probability qualifier. These documentation gains and newly introduced mathematical inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
